messages:
ashley: reported by customer (Acme) - users hitting a 400 from Google on the OAuth callback. They see `error=invalid_request&error_description=state+mismatch` right after Google redirects back. Happening consistently for a specific app client_id. Repro steps attached below.

kevin: can you paste the full redirect_uri that's being used? also any request logs from our callback endpoint (headers + querystring) would help.

ashley: here's the redir we captured from the browser dev tools. note the state looks long and contains encoded JSON: 

```
https://app.redwood.example.com/oauth/callback?code=4/0AY0e-g6...&state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6Il9fQ29tcGxleERhdGEtZW5jb2RlZCIsInBrc2NlIjoibG9uZ192ZXJpZmllciJ9%3D
```

ashley: server logs from callback (nginx + app) show querystring truncated at ~1024 chars. snippet from our access log (redacted):

```
GET /oauth/callback?code=4%2F...&state=eyJzdGF0ZSI6Il9fQ29tc...  200  0.123
```

support-bot: automatic note: customer on plan: enterprise-dedicated; region: us-west1.

kevin: interesting. two hypotheses: 1) state param is getting truncated by proxy (we saw similar when querystrings exceeded buffer limits), 2) PKCE verifier/state stored client-side lost (eg. Safari private mode) and state doesn't match stored session. which browser did the customer use?

ashley: customer reproduces on Chrome desktop and Chrome on mobile (android). They said it happens after they sign into Google and a large redirect URL is returned (we think we embed extra app params into state). Not Safari.

maria: I dug into identity service: we generate a state blob that includes an internal nonce + the PKCE code_verifier (base64url). We URL-encode the entire blob and expect it to roundtrip. If the proxy truncates querystrings > 1024 there's a guaranteed mismatch. We also recently enabled an internal monitoring header insertion at the proxy that increased average querystring size for some customers.

kevin: can we repro locally by crafting a long state? I'll try to simulate with curl and our staging proxy.

kevin: repro steps I ran:

1) start local app with same redirect path (/oauth/callback)
2) craft state payload: `{\"state\":\"${'x'.repeat(1500)}\",\"pkce\":\"${'y'.repeat(400)}\"}` then `encodeURIComponent` -> attach as `?state=`
3) hit `https://staging-proxy.local/oauth/callback?state=...` -> observed truncation in access log, app only received ~1024 chars.

kevin: minimal nginx reproduction: our proxy set `proxy_buffer_size 8k` but `large_client_header_buffers 4 8k` may be unrelated. the truncation path looks like `uwsgi_param QUERY_STRING $query_string;` with an older module that limits to 1024.

maria: good catch. also note: some customers embed JSON in state which explodes length. we should stop stuffing the PKCE code_verifier into state; put it in a server-side session (or store in ephemeral backend keyed by a short nonce).

ashley: customer impact: Acme users can't complete Google login at scale; workaround suggested to them was to shorten state by removing nonessential fields and move the large payload to an intermediate short id that our app can resolve. they asked for a permanent fix.

infra-oncall: immediate mitigation options:
- increase proxy querystring buffer thresholds and bump the module that limits QUERY_STRING handling (we have a patch ready in infra repo).
- add fallback: if state param missing/short, try to read a base64 payload from POST body? (not ideal)

kevin: suggested code change in identity service: stop serializing pkce verifier into the state blob. instead, generate a 16-byte random nonce, store {pkce_verifier, nonce, created_at} in redis with ttl=5m, and put only the nonce in the state payload. that reduces state length massively.

maria: agree. patch to identity service opened: `reduce-state-payload-186543` (PR link: internal). includes migration and tests.

maria: nginx patch: update proxy config in staging and prod-canary to set `proxy_read_timeout` and `proxy_buffer_size` higher and remove the legacy module that truncated `QUERY_STRING`. will roll canary to 10% first.

ashley: customer asked for ETA. what's realistic?

infra-oncall: timeline: staging patch in 2 hours, prod-canary in 6 hours, full rollout after 24-48h verification if no regressions. urgent rollback plan in the runbook if proxy errors spike.

kevin: also adding a quick server-side guard: if state param doesn't parse as expected, log full request (redacted) and return a helpful error page for customers with a short copy: `We couldn't complete sign-in. Please retry or contact support and include this reference ID: <id>`. That will speed debugging for support.

maria: one more edge-case: GitHub OAuth can return a `state` with `+` characters (space) if not encoded properly; ensure we treat `+` as `%2B` vs space. added parsing test.

ashley: notes to send to customer: explain cause (proxy truncated long state causing mismatch), short-term workaround (shorten state or use short nonce), ETA for fix (canary in 6h, full rollout 24-48h), and ask them to confirm if they can switch to a client update to stop embedding big objects into `state`.

kevin: logging snippet we'll add to identity service (example):

```
if (!isValidState(req.query.state)) {
  log.warn('oauth.state.invalid', { len: req.query.state?.length || 0, truncated: maybeTruncated(req) });
  return renderErrorPage(res, 400, 'state_mismatch_detected', { ref: uuid() });
}
```

ashley: saved convo and replied to customer with summary + temporary mitigation steps. I'll update this thread after canary results. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: canary deployed to 10% at 1865435400 (followup). monitoring dashboards will watch 5xx and latency.

ashley: thx everyone. keeping this thread open until full rollout.
